pkix-truststore crate landed. Workspace member at 0.0.0 per stub convention.

Public API (all gated by crate features none, since this is std-only):
- from_pem(&[u8]) -> Vec<TrustAnchor>
- from_der(&[u8]) -> TrustAnchor
- from_der_iter(IntoIterator<Item: AsRef<[u8]>>) -> Vec<TrustAnchor>  -- canonical adapter entry point
- from_pem_file(impl AsRef<Path>) -> Vec<TrustAnchor>
- from_der_file(impl AsRef<Path>) -> TrustAnchor
- Error (#[non_exhaustive]) with Io / Pem / Der / NoCertificates / MalformedAnchor(usize)
- pub use pkix_path::TrustAnchor

Implementation builds on x509_cert::Certificate::load_pem_chain (gated by der/x509-cert `pem` feature). RFC 7468 strict PEM decoding via pem-rfc7468 underneath.

Real-world quirks handled (with tests in tests/fixtures.rs):
- multi-cert concatenated PEM bundles (Debian /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt fixture, 147 anchors)
- header comments before first cert
- OpenSSL Subject/Issuer/Serial metadata lines between certs
- leading UTF-8 BOM (own preprocessing; load_pem_chain does not handle this)
- CRLF / mixed line endings
- trailing whitespace after last cert
- back-to-back END/BEGIN with no blank line
- empty input / unknown PEM label / truncated block / garbage base64 -> NoCertificates or Pem/Der error
- empty / out-of-bound entries in from_der_iter -> NoCertificates / MalformedAnchor(usize)

Known limitations documented in rustdoc:
- trailing NON-whitespace content after last END is rejected (matches load_pem_chain).
- unknown PEM labels (PRIVATE KEY, X509 CRL, ...) are an error, not silently skipped.

Pinned upstream bug found and worked around: x509_cert::Certificate::load_pem_chain panics with subtract-with-overflow on empty input. Filed as PKIX-wzmg.

Tests: 6 unit + 21 integration + 1 doc test. Oracle for the Debian fixture cert count is `grep -c "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----"` (re-derived in-test from the fixture bytes, NOT from from_pem). Oracle for single-cert PEM <-> DER equality is OpenSSL's `openssl x509 -outform DER`. Synthetic quirk tests build their inputs deterministically from known-good cert1.pem bytes.

Acceptance deferred:
- Alpine and Fedora ca-bundle fixtures filed as follow-up PKIX-zydl. Dev environment had only Debian's bundle offline; per the no-fabrication policy, missing fixtures were filed rather than synthesised.

AGENTS.md and CHANGELOG.md updated with project stance and crate inventory.

- cargo +1.73 build / test clean (MSRV)
- RUSTDOCFLAGS="--cfg docsrs -D warnings" cargo +nightly doc --no-deps --all-features clean
- typos pkix-truststore/ clean

description:
## Why

`pkix-path::validate_path` takes `&[TrustAnchor]` and the caller wires up loading. Currently every consumer reinvents the PEM/DER parse. A small dedicated crate eliminates the duplication and gives the workspace a canonical place to grow trust-store features later (system stores, etc.) without polluting `pkix-path`.

## Scope (Tier 1)

A new workspace member `pkix-truststore/` providing pure-Rust loading of trust anchors from caller-supplied bytes or paths. No platform FFI, no compiled-in trust data, no network fetching.

The Tier 1 core is also the **canonical landing point for adapter crates** (see "Sources deferred to adapter crates" below). Adapters fetch DER bytes from non-file sources (HSMs, OS APIs, cloud KMS) and feed them into `from_der_iter`.

## API surface (initial sketch)

```rust
// Bytes-in, anchors-out — no I/O, deterministic, testable.
pub fn from_pem(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<TrustAnchor>, Error>;
pub fn from_der(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<TrustAnchor, Error>;

// The canonical adapter entry point. Consumers and adapter crates that have
// already obtained DER bytes from any source (file read, HSM API, OS keychain
// API, cloud KMS, network protocol) feed them through this. Single entry point
// keeps the validation/parsing logic centralised in pkix-truststore core; the
// caller is responsible only for getting the bytes from the source.
pub fn from_der_iter<I, B>(iter: I) -> Result<Vec<TrustAnchor>, Error>
where
    I: IntoIterator<Item = B>,
    B: AsRef<[u8]>;

// Convenience: file I/O wrappers (gated on `std` feature, default-on).
pub fn from_pem_file(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Vec<TrustAnchor>, Error>;
pub fn from_der_file(path: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<TrustAnchor, Error>;

// Re-export for ergonomics so consumers do not need a separate `pkix-path` import.
pub use pkix_path::TrustAnchor;

// Crate-local error type. Minimal variants:
pub enum Error {
    Io(std::io::Error),
    Pem(/* pem-rfc7468 or pem error */),
    Der(der::Error),
    NoCertificates,        // bundle parsed cleanly but contained zero certs
    MalformedAnchor(usize), // index of the offending cert in the bundle
}
```

The PEM loader returns `Vec<TrustAnchor>` because PEM bundles routinely contain many concatenated certs (Debian `ca-certificates.crt`, etc.). The DER loader returns one because DER does not concatenate cleanly. The iter loader generalises the multi-DER case for adapters.

## Real-world bundle quirks the parser must tolerate

- Header comment blocks before any `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----`.
- OpenSSL-style "subject + issuer + serial" comment lines between certs (Debian bundle format).
- CRLF line endings; mixed line endings within one file.
- Stray BOM at file start.
- Trailing whitespace / blank lines after the last cert.
- Multiple `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` blocks back to back with no blank line.

The `pem-rfc7468` crate (RustCrypto) handles most of this strictly per RFC 7468; `pem` is more permissive. Choice between them is the implementer s call — the bead does not pre-commit. Test against real-world bundles (Debian, Alpine, Fedora ca-certificates outputs) before settling.

## Explicit out of scope (project stance: no baked-in trust data, no baked-in trust source)

These are deliberate non-goals for this bead. Filing follow-up beads is fine; do not bundle into this one:

- **Compiled-in Mozilla CA bundle.** The `webpki-roots` model is rejected for this project — trust data is deployment configuration, not library content. If a Mozilla snapshot is needed, it lives in a separate crate or as build-time data the consumer supplies.
- **Per-anchor trust policy.** NSS-style trust flags ("trusted for serverAuth only," "distrust after date X," constraint patterns) are a substantial data-model extension that affects `pkix-path::TrustAnchor` itself. Out of scope; revisit when a concrete consumer asks for it.

### Sources deferred to adapter crates

The unifying currency for trust anchors is DER bytes. For sources where the platform/library/cloud exposes DER via an API rather than a file, the canonical pattern is a separate opt-in adapter crate that calls the source-specific API and feeds bytes into `pkix_truststore::from_der_iter(...)`. Adapter crates are opt-in dependencies of the consumer — they are not part of `pkix-truststore` core.

**Adapter crates with placeholder beads filed:**

- **PKIX-8h87** — `pkix-truststore-system` — OS-native trust stores: macOS Security framework, Windows CryptoAPI, iOS Keychain, Android KeyStore, Linux/BSD distro CA bundle paths. The `rustls-native-certs` analog.
- **PKIX-p8vz** — `pkix-truststore-pkcs11` — PKCS#11 tokens: HSMs (Yubico HSM, Thales, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, SafeNet), YubiKey PIV, smart cards (PIV/CAC), TPM 2.0 via `tpm2-pkcs11`, SoftHSM for testing.

**Adapter crates plausible — file when there is concrete demand:**

- `pkix-truststore-aws` — AWS ACM Private CA (`ListCertificateAuthorities` + `GetCertificateAuthorityCertificate`), AWS Secrets Manager, SSM Parameter Store.
- `pkix-truststore-azure` — Azure Key Vault, Azure Trusted Signing.
- `pkix-truststore-gcp` — GCP Certificate Authority Service, GCP Secret Manager.
- `pkix-truststore-vault` — HashiCorp Vault PKI secrets engine.
- `pkix-truststore-nss` — NSS API bindings (direct `cert9.db` SQLite parsing is fragile across NSS versions; the supported access path is the NSS C API).
- `pkix-truststore-est` — RFC 7030 EST client (network-protocol trust anchor delivery).
- `pkix-truststore-scep` — Cisco/IETF SCEP (similar shape to EST).
- `pkix-truststore-cmp` — RFC 4210 Certificate Management Protocol.

Each adapter is a thin "API call → `Vec<DER bytes>` → `pkix_truststore::from_der_iter(...)` → `Vec<TrustAnchor>`" wrapper. They compose trivially: a consumer can union anchors from multiple sources by concatenating the resulting `Vec<TrustAnchor>`s.

## Implementation notes

- `pkix-truststore/Cargo.toml`: workspace member, `version = "0.0.0"` initially per the stub-crate convention used by `pkix-revocation-http`/`pkix-ct`/`pkix-composite`/`pkix-ac`, bumped to `0.1.0` (or `0.2.1` matching workspace) on first publish.
- Dependencies: `pkix-path`, `der`, `x509-cert`, plus one PEM dep (`pem-rfc7468` recommended; defer the choice to the implementer with a 1-paragraph rationale in the PR).
- MSRV: workspace 1.73.
- `no_std`: no. PEM parsing wants heap; file I/O needs std. The crate is std-only.
- Re-export `TrustAnchor` from `pkix-path` so consumers do not need both imports.
- Tests: load Debian `ca-certificates.crt`, Alpine `ca-certificates.crt`, Fedora `ca-bundle.crt`, plus negative-test fixtures (truncated PEM, unknown PEM label, garbage bytes, empty file, BOM-prefixed file, CRLF mixed with LF). Bundle the test fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`.
- Test `from_der_iter` with an iterator of arbitrary length (zero, one, many) and with `&[u8]`, `Vec<u8>`, and borrowed-from-pem-blocks input shapes — adapters will pass it whatever they have.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pkix-truststore/` workspace member exists with `0.0.0` version (matches stub-crate convention).
- [ ] Public API: `from_pem`, `from_der`, `from_der_iter`, `from_pem_file`, `from_der_file`, `Error`, re-exported `TrustAnchor`.
- [ ] Roundtrip tests against at least three real-world distro CA bundles (Debian, Alpine, Fedora).
- [ ] Negative tests: every documented quirk (BOM, mixed line endings, header comments, etc.) handled correctly.
- [ ] `from_der_iter` exercised with empty, single-element, and many-element iterators in tests.
- [ ] No platform-specific code, no FFI, no `[target.<platform>.dependencies]`, no compiled-in trust data, no compiled-in trust source.
- [ ] `cargo fmt` / `cargo clippy --all-features -p pkix-truststore -- -D warnings` clean.
- [ ] `typos pkix-truststore/` clean.
- [ ] README and rustdoc explicitly state the "no baked-in trust data, no baked-in trust source" project stance and point at PKIX-8h87, PKIX-p8vz, and the deferred Tier 2/3/4 work.
- [ ] AGENTS.md updated to note `pkix-truststore` exists, its scope, and the project stance.

## Decomposition recommendation

Probably one PR. The whole crate is ~300–500 LOC including tests and fixtures. If decomposition is wanted:

1. Skeleton + `Error` + `from_der` + `from_der_iter` (adapter pattern foundation).
2. `from_pem` + bundle quirks handling + real-world distro fixtures.
3. File I/O wrappers + integration with `tests/fixtures/`.
4. AGENTS.md + README documentation pass.

But (1)–(3) are tightly coupled enough that one PR with reviewable commits is cleaner than four PRs.
notes: Filed in response to architectural review of workspace crate structure. User scope decision: Tier 1 only (PEM/DER bytes+files), no platform stores, no baked-in trust data. The "no baked-in" stance is a project-level constraint — record in AGENTS.md when the crate lands.
